We are to act as a software developer implementing this increment. The specification is for Spring XD (Spring XD is a project for data ingestion, real-time analytics, batch processing, etc., built on Spring Boot, Spring Integration, etc.). The user stories are:

U1: Delete queues/topics with optional attribute in stream destroy command (RabbitMQ cleanup). Involves RabbitAdmin, RabbitManagementTemplate, considerations about producers, queues, fanout exchange, and where to implement (admin, container, plugin).

U2: Notify when exception thrown in a module, tap into error channel for each stream/module.

U3: Security configurations for REST endpoints (Spring Security, Spring Boot). Research, design, developer experience (credentials, DSL shell, Admin UI).

U4: Document keys like ${xd.stream.name}, ${xd.job.name}, ${xd.container.???} available to users.

U5: OOTB MVC-aware HTTP module with embedded Tomcat, leveraging spring-mvc and spring-security, richer content-type support, full header mapping.

U6: Common polling strategy on client side to detect status changes of jobs/streams; ideally server-side events propagation between containers and admin-server to notify UI clients.

U7: SFTP source module using Spring Integration SFTP Adapter. Consider testing infrastructure.

U8: Native ElasticSearch sink module for aggregating, searching, analyzing data in real-time.

We need to break down into activities. Since these are user stories, each may require multiple activities: design, implementation, testing, documentation, etc. We'll create a WBS.

We must make assumptions where spec is lacking.

Let's list technical and design decisions and assumptions first.

Technical and Design Decisions:
1. For U1: Implement queue/topic cleanup as part of stream destroy command with --clean option. Use RabbitAdmin.getQueueProperties() to check consumers. Cleanup will be performed on the container side (since admin may not know cluster). Use RabbitManagementTemplate if available, else direct REST API. Handle fanout exchange cleanup after queues/topics removed. Consider producers and queues with data: maybe only delete if no messages? But spec says "Consider the possibility of producers and/or queues still containing data". We'll assume we delete regardless, but log warning. Or we could add a force option. We'll decide: delete queues and exchanges only if no messages, else skip with warning. But spec says "clean-up the associated queues/topics". We'll implement as: when --clean is specified, attempt to delete queues, bindings, and exchanges; if queues have messages, log error and skip deletion of that queue. For fanout exchange, delete if no bindings left.

2. For U2: Implement an error channel per stream/module. Use Spring Integration's error handling: when a module throws an exception, send error message to a dedicated error channel (e.g., "error.<streamName>.<moduleIndex>"). Users can subscribe to this channel. We'll need to modify module deployment to wire error channels.

3. For U3: Security for REST endpoints. Use Spring Security with Spring Boot's auto-configuration. Provide configuration properties for authentication (e.g., basic auth, OAuth2). Secure all REST endpoints by default. DSL shell and Admin UI will need to handle authentication (e.g., pass credentials). We'll implement a security configuration module that can be enabled via property.

4. For U4: Documentation task. Identify all available keys (xd.stream.name, xd.job.name, xd.container.id, etc.) and document them in the reference guide.

5. For U5: Create a new HTTP module (e.g., http-mvc) that uses Spring MVC with embedded Tomcat. This module will replace or complement existing HTTP source. It will support full header mapping, content-type negotiation, and Spring Security integration. We'll base it on Spring Integration's HTTP inbound gateway but with MVC capabilities.

6. For U6: Implement a polling mechanism on client side (shell, UI) to check status of deployments. Also implement server-side event propagation using Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher or a message bus to broadcast deployment status changes. Containers and admin server will publish events; clients can subscribe via WebSocket or long polling.

7. For U7: Develop SFTP source module using Spring Integration SFTP inbound channel adapter. Provide configuration options (host, port, username, password/key, remote directory, local directory, file pattern, etc.). Write integration tests with a test SFTP server (e.g., using Apache MINA SSHD or a Docker container).

8. For U8: Develop ElasticSearch sink module using Spring Data Elasticsearch or Spring Integration Elasticsearch adapter. Support indexing documents, bulk operations, configuration of cluster, index, type, etc. Write integration tests with an embedded Elasticsearch or test container.

U8: Elasticsearch sink module implemented using Spring Data Elasticsearch with support for indexing, bulk operations, and configuration of cluster/index. Test infrastructure uses Testcontainers for Elasticsearch.
assumptions: Development uses Java 17+, Spring Boot 3.x, Spring Framework 6.x, Spring Integration 6.x.
Project built with Maven/Gradle; existing module structure for sources, sinks, processors.
Testing infrastructure supports Testcontainers for RabbitMQ, SFTP, Elasticsearch.
Team is familiar with Spring XD codebase.
Effort estimates are for a single developer per activity; total effort is sum of individual efforts.
User stories implemented sequentially but activities within a story may overlap.

No major refactoring of existing modules required beyond what's described.
